questions.q: What is the central idea of the passage?
options: Intuition is a more reliable guide than analysis for new problems
Breaking problems down to what is truly irreducible lets you build new solutions
Philosophers like Plato already solved the problem of foundational truth
Copying proven methods from successful people is the fastest route to innovation
questions.explain: It describes first principles thinking as separating what is absolutely true from assumptions and building from the essentials.

questions.q: According to Musk, what share of a typical rocket's price is the cost of its materials?
questions.explain: Musk found the materials cost of a rocket was around two percent of the typical price.

questions.q: What did Musk say battery materials would cost per kilowatt-hour on the commodity market?
questions.explain: He contrasted the historical $600 per kWh with about $80 for the raw materials.

questions.q: What first principle of a successful website did Jonah Peretti identify for BuzzFeed?
questions.explain: Peretti figured the first principle was wide distribution, publishing what people want to read and share.

questions.q: Why does the author suggest people dislike the repeated 'why' game?
options: It reminds them of childhood punishments
It is usually asked by people with bad intentions
It exposes that they often do not actually know the reason
It always leads to answers that are too complicated
questions.explain: The author says after one or two questions we are often lost, confronted with our own ignorance, and resort to self-defense.
